Shri Satish Chandra Shirvastava, learned counsel for t  No.1.
 Shri Mayank Upadhyay, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER 01.
With consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

02. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 6/3/2024 passed in MACC No.1056/2022 by the 2nd Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.3,81,838/-
has been awarded to the appellant / claimant by way of compensation.

03. As per the appellant, on 11.6.2022 at about 4.00 PM appellant was going towards Dewas with his friend on his Activa Scooter having number M.P. 09 UV 1229 slowly from their safe side, and when they reached Sanwer road Tiraha, AB Road, Mangliya then the respondent No.1, the driver/owner NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20981 2 MA-4651-2024 of the offending vehicle Eicher Truck bearing registration number GJ 27/TT 6225 drove the truck in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against the vehicle of the appellant, as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
04. Thereafter the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to him.
The application was contested by respondent No.2 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded amount of Rs.1,98,000/- for sustaining permanent disability at 40% and after award further compensation in other heads a total sum of Rs.3,81,838/- was awarded.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount of compensation is very meager in all the heads.

He submits that in view of the permanent disability sustained by the appellant at 65%
which is duly proved by the appellant on the strength of statement of Dr. Kush Bandi (PW.2), the claims tribunal should have considered the permanent disability at 65% itself.
He also submits that even the income of the appellant has not correctly been assessed.

It has been taken into consideration at Rs.7500/- from the date of accident as per the Collector guidelines ie., on 11/6/2022 whereas as per the State Legal Services Authority guidelines, the minimum wages for an unskilled labour at the relevant time was Rs.9125/- per month.

On the other heads of compensation it is submitted that looking to the advance age of the appellant which according to the appellant is 70 years and according to the findings of the claims tribunal is 79 years, compensation for special diet, attendant, transportation and pain and suffering should have been much NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20981 3 MA-4651-2024 higher then what has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
Thus, a prayer has been made for enhancement of the compensation.

06. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 / Insurance Co. submits that in fact, if the Entry No.21 of Schedule of the Employee's Compensation Act is seen, then the permanent disability sustained by the appellant in his right leg is only at 50% in view of the fact that the amputation below knee with stump exceeding 25 Cms.
Thus the claims tribunal has rather taken the permanent disability on higher side.
Thus he submits that the compensation in any case is more than adequate and thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.

07. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
08.
It is seen from the record that there is no dispute about the injury sustained by the appellant and amputation of his right leg.
The only question is regarding the assessment of income, whether should have been taken at Rs.9125/- or as determined by the claims tribunal.

It is also to be seen that whether the permanent disability is to be taken in accordance with the Schedule of Employee's Compensation Act or according to the statement rendered by Dr. Kush Bandi (PW.2).

The consideration of the claims tribunal about the the permanent disability of the appellant appears to be correct and proper and if the arguments of the counsel for the Insurance Co. is accepted, then the the permanent disability is to be taken at 50%, which has been taken by the claims tribunal as 40%.
As regards the income, it is indeed correct that the M.P. State Legal Services Authority has prescribed minimum wages for unskilled labour as Rs.9125/- per month at the relevant point of time.

09. In view of the above circumstances, instead of requantifying the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20981 4 MA-4651-2024 compensation, it is considered proper that a lump sum amount of Rs.1,50,000 is awarded to the appellant over and above the compensation already awarded by the claims tribunal.

Thus the appellant is directed to be paid an amount Rs.1,50,000/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
10.
The appeal is accordingly disposed off.
